summary: Duplicate function execution after mid-flight JWT refresh in mixed Node/Go orchestration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external tool/function invocations when their orchestration flow uses a Node.js client to drive a long-lived streaming session and then delegates heavy processing to Go-based workers. The duplicates happen when the Node client performs an automatic JWT refresh mid-stream and a retry path in the Go worker re-sends a previously-confirmed function call.

Impact:
- Observed duplicate side effects: duplicate database writes and duplicate webhook posts to downstream services.
- Customer Brightloop Labs reports data integrity issues and has paused traffic to the affected route.
- Affects production traffic in us-east region using redwood/gptx-2.7b.

Environment:
- Customer orchestration: Node 18.x client (ts-sdk v1.12.4) -> Redwood streaming API -> Go worker (go-sdk v0.9.7) consuming function-call callbacks.
- Auth: short-lived JWTs (~5m expiry) rotated by customer's auth service midway through long requests.
- Redirection/Edge: traffic passes through an internal proxy layer that rewrites a subset of headers.

High-level hypothesis:
Race between client-side JWT refresh (Node) and Go worker retry logic that replays unacknowledged function-calls. During the refresh, idempotency metadata is dropped or normalized differently across the Node and Go SDKs, so server cannot correlate the re-send with the prior acknowledged execution.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a long-running chat streaming session from Node client (ts-sdk v1.12.4) with two function-enabled messages: step A (internal confirmation) and step B (external webhook).
2) Trigger a synchronous handoff to a Go worker by sending the stream delta to the worker service which calls back into Redwood function endpoints.
3) Simulate JWT refresh on the Node client mid-stream (replace token with a freshly minted JWT while stream still open).
4) Force a transient network hiccup between Go worker and Redwood (drop packet, small RTT spike) to cause the Go worker to retry the function call that had previously been acknowledged by the Node client.
5) Observe duplicate external webhook posts and duplicate DB writes for the same orchestration ID.

Notes: customer provided a minimal repro harness that follows these steps; we reproduced locally with their harness with lower frequency but matching behavior.

investigation_notes: Confirmed repro with customer's harness when token rotation implemented as mid-stream client-side JWT replacement.
Observed idempotency key present on Node client send but absent on the retried request from Go worker (SDK header mapping issue).
Proxy layer normalizes Authorization header differently for new token which leads to different canonicalization of idempotency header in Go SDK (suspect header truncation/sequence).

Server receives two distinct request fingerprints: one with idempotency-key=tx-7c9b and one with idempotency-key missing; fallback route accepted second execution because server-side dedupe requires explicit key.
Race window: ~3s between Node refresh and worker retry — within customer-observed window for duplicates.
No evidence of server-side double-execute unrelated to key mismatch; i.e., when keys match we see correct dedupe behavior.
Go SDK v0.9.7 uses 'X-Idempotency-Key' header; Node ts-sdk v1.12.4 uses 'Idemp-Key' header name in this customer's customization; proxy mapping misaligns them during auth header rewrite.
comments: [2026-03-09] Brightloop Support: We saw two webhook posts at 15:05:16 and 15:05:18 for the same orchestration ID. Can you confirm if Redwood retried?

[2026-03-09] Support (Aisha Khan): Thanks — attaching logs and asking for a repro harness. Please provide exact SDK versions and any custom header mappers.
(Added request for RT traces)
[2026-03-09] Brightloop: Sent repro harness and proxy config. They replace Authorization header in an edge sidecar and canonicalize header names to lowercase.
[2026-03-10] Support: Reproduced locally. Escalated to Eng and linked INT-4412. Assigning Diego Morales to investigate cross-sdk header mapping and token rotation interaction.

[2026-03-11] Eng (Diego Morales): Observed that header canonicalization in proxy removed capitalization used by Node SDK; will instrument server-side matching to tolerate both header names as short-term mitigation.

[2026-03-12] Eng (Diego Morales): Created PRs to normalize idempotency header names across SDKs and server-side acceptance (see related_github_prs). Working on patch release and guidance note for customers about token-rotation best practices.
resolution:
(Work in progress) Temporary mitigation: advise customer to ensure their edge proxy preserves original idempotency header name and forwards 'X-Idempotency-Key' or canonical 'Idempotency' headers unchanged during Authorization rewrites. We instrumented server to accept both canonical header forms to reduce matches missing the key.

Planned permanent fix:
- Normalize idempotency header names at SDK layer (node & go) and add a server-side canonicalization layer so that idempotency keys are matched regardless of header case/name variants. PRs opened: sdk-node#788, serving-runtime#1293.
- Add unit/integration tests simulating mid-stream JWT rotation and proxy header rewrite to catch regressions.
- Postmortem runbook update: include 'token refresh mid-stream' as a known risky pattern and recommended avoidance steps (prefer refresh only between sessions or use refresh tokens that do not replace in-flight Authorization slices).

Follow-ups assigned:
- INT-4412: update server-side dedupe matching and add metrics for idempotency misses.
- SUP-992234 (action): provide Brightloop with a patched node sdk build and config checklist.
workarounds: Customer workaround applied: disable proxy header canonicalization for idempotency headers and preserve original header names until patched SDKs are released.

Short-term server-side mitigation: accept both X-Idempotency-Key and Idemp-Key header names and treat missing idempotency on retried requests as potential duplicate if another fingerprint matches within 30s window (conservative).
